title: Stonean covers of compact Hausdorff spaces
statement:
Let $T$ be a compact Hausdorff space (for instance profinite) and let $D$ be its underlying
set with the discrete topology. Let $\beta D$ be the set of ultrafilters on $D$, topologized
by the basis of sets $\widehat E=\{\mathfrak p\in\beta D: E\in\mathfrak p\}$ for $E\subset D$.

1. $\beta D$ is compact Hausdorff, the sets $\widehat E$ are clopen, and $D\to\beta D$,
   $d\mapsto$ (principal ultrafilter at $d$), has dense image.
2. $\beta D$ is extremally disconnected; hence (by [det-pe-stonean-projective]) it is
   profinite and projective.
3. The map $\pi\colon\beta D\to T$ sending $\mathfrak p$ to the unique limit in $T$ of the
   ultrafilter $\mathfrak p$ is continuous and surjective, and it extends the identity of
   the underlying set.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis] with $S=D$. Its maximal proper filters are exactly the ultrafilters in the statement, and its basic set $[E]$ is $\widehat E$. Thus $\beta D$ is compact Hausdorff and the $\widehat E$ form a clopen basis.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1: compact Hausdorff ultrafilter topology and clopen basis

proof.text: Write $p(d)=\{E\subseteq D:d\in E\}$ for the principal ultrafilter. This family is a proper filter; if $A$ does not contain $d$, its complement belongs to $p(d)$, so adjoining $A$ would force the empty set into the filter. Hence $p(d)$ is maximal proper. A nonempty basic open $\widehat E$ has $E\ne\varnothing$, since a proper filter never contains the empty set. Choose $d\in E$; then $p(d)\in\widehat E$. By the basis in [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis], every nonempty open contains such a basic open and hence a principal ultrafilter. This proves density.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, last sentence: density of principal ultrafilters

proof.text: By the clopen basis of [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis], write an arbitrary open set as $O=\bigcup_i\widehat{E_i}$ and set $E=\bigcup_i E_i$. Upward closure of filters gives $O\subseteq\widehat E$, so $\overline O\subseteq\widehat E$ because $\widehat E$ is closed. Conversely, if $\mathfrak p\in\widehat E$ and $\widehat F$ is a basic neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$, then $E\cap F\in\mathfrak p$ and thus $E\cap F\ne\varnothing$. Choose $d\in E\cap F$ and an index $i$ with $d\in E_i$. Then $p(d)\in\widehat F\cap\widehat{E_i}\subseteq\widehat F\cap O$. Every neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$ contains a basic one, so it meets $O$; therefore $\mathfrak p\in\overline O$. Consequently $\overline O=\widehat E$ is open, proving extremal disconnectedness. If the family is empty, both sides are empty, since no proper filter contains $\varnothing$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2: the explicit equality between the closure of an open union and a basic clopen

proof.text: The space $\beta D$ is compact Hausdorff by step 1 and extremally disconnected by step 3. In [det-pe-stonean-projective], implication $1\Rightarrow2$ gives projectivity for continuous surjections of compact Hausdorff spaces, and the final assertion gives total disconnectedness and profiniteness.

source.place: Statement clause 2, final implication: profiniteness and projectivity from det-pe-stonean-projective

proof.text: Let $f:D\to T$ be the identity on underlying sets. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-continuous-extension] with $S=D$ and $K=T$ to obtain a continuous map $g:\beta D\to T$ such that $g(p(d))=d$ for every $d\in D$. Its hypotheses hold because $T$ is compact Hausdorff; $D$ is merely a set and no continuity of $f$ is required.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: continuous extension of the identity from the underlying discrete set

proof.text: For any $\mathfrak p\in\beta D$ and any open neighbourhood $V$ of $g(\mathfrak p)$, continuity of $g$ makes $g^{-1}(V)$ open and containing $\mathfrak p$. By the basis in [lem-weil-pbc-ultrafilter-compact-hausdorff-basis], choose $E\in\mathfrak p$ with $\widehat E\subseteq g^{-1}(V)$. For every $d\in E$, the principal ultrafilter $p(d)$ lies in $\widehat E$, and hence $d=g(p(d))\in V$ by step 5. Thus $E\subseteq V$ on the underlying set $D$, so $V\in\mathfrak p$ by upward closure. Since every neighbourhood contains an open neighbourhood, $\mathfrak p$ converges to $g(\mathfrak p)$ in $T$. This identifies the limit for the actual map $g$ just constructed; no particular choice of extension is assumed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, first sentence: existence of an ultrafilter limit, here verified directly for the continuous extension

proof.text: If the same proper ultrafilter converged to two distinct points of $T$, Hausdorffness would give disjoint open neighbourhoods of those points. Both would belong to the ultrafilter, forcing their empty intersection to belong to it, a contradiction. Thus step 6 gives the unique limit of every $\mathfrak p$, and $\pi=g$ is exactly the map in the statement. It is continuous by step 5. The equality $\pi(p(t))=t$ from step 5 proves both extension of the underlying identity and surjectivity. These arguments also cover $T=D=\varnothing$: there is no proper filter on the empty set, so $\beta D=\varnothing$ and the empty map is surjective.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: uniqueness, agreement on principal ultrafilters, continuity and surjectivity
